blocks.text: 1 January. Buenos Aires and a Food Tour

After breakfast, we set out on a sightseeing tour of the capital.

You'll visit central neighbourhoods as well as La Boca and San Telmo.

San Telmo has plenty of cafés and restaurants.

If you're interested in antiques, take a look around Plaza Dorrego.

The route also takes in Plaza de Mayo and the Casa Rosada, a building closely associated with the history of Evita Perón.

After sightseeing, we take a food tour of Buenos Aires.

Return to the hotel after the tour.
Pink facade of the Casa Rosada beyond a bed of yellow flowers in Buenos Aires, Argentina
Buenos Aires: the Casa Rosada beyond flowers and flagpoles

After breakfast, transfer to the airport for the flight to Bariloche.

On arrival, transfer to the Llao Llao Hotel.

Bariloche sits among the lakes, Andes mountains and forests of Nahuel Huapi National Park.

The city is known as a ski resort and a centre for chocolate making.

Natural sights around the city include Cerro Campanario, Playa Bonita, the Llao Llao Peninsula, Lake Moreno, Huemul Island and El Trébol Bay.

The area is also home to San Eduardo Chapel.

In winter, the slopes of Cerro Catedral, at around 2,388 m, and Cerro Otto, at around 1,405 m, are used for winter recreation.

In summer, the area is suited to walking, fishing and trips to the myrtle groves.

In spring, greenery and flowers spread across the valleys and lakeshores. In autumn, the forests turn red, orange and brown.

Stay at the Llao Llao Hotel.
